To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Proton therapy (PT) and intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) are equally effective in treating prostate cancer; (2) The dosimetry of PT is better than IMRT; and (3) The dosimetric benefits of PT are offset by greater inter- and intrafractional motion.
The effects of interfractional variations on proton therapy for prostate cancer are similar to intensity modulated radiation therapy (IMRT).
